detail.description: What was found, or why it was not checked

id.description: A signal id, or a question git alone cannot answer

before.description: The value before, as the `config-integrity` finding shows it

change_index.description: The change's position, 0 for the newest audited change

cites.description: Issue references in a directive's reason, as written; omitted when none

class.description: `process`: a waiver of a process rule (`no-issue`); `detector`: a waiver of a finding

count.description: List entries gained or lost, or baseline findings added

detail.description: Why a configuration or baseline could not be compared

edited.description: A loosening whose own change also tightened the same option: an edited entry, which `config-integrity` counts as lost unless it can prove it tighter. Omitted when false

evidence.description: `claimed`: text that asks for an exception; `applied`: a tree change that is one

file.description: Where the exception is: the inline marker's file, the baseline, or `discipline.toml`

gate.description: Gate id, or the configuration table a loosening is under; null for a directive this binary does not map to a gate

hidden.description: The directive was inside an HTML comment

key.description: The configuration option a loosening changed

lifted.description: With `--replay`, for a finding waiver: whether the replayed check applied it to lift a finding (then `evidence` is `applied`). Omitted when the replay did not judge the change, for `no-issue`, and for inline markers

pr.description: Pull request number, from the subject's `(#N)`

ratification.description: A protected edit's ratification, judged as `ratified-paths` judges it, with `--forge`. The ratifier's login is not carried

created.description: When the ratifying comment was posted, seconds since the Unix epoch

issue_repo.description: The repository of the issue carrying the ratifying comment

why.description: Why it is unratified or not checked

reason.description: The directive's reason text: only under `--reasons`

reason_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the directive's reason, to group reuse without the text

sha.description: Full commit id of the change

subject.description: The change's subject line, as its author wrote it

tier.description: Who controls the input: `A` git objects on the audited branch, `C` text the change's author wrote

time.description: Commit time, seconds since the Unix epoch

changes.description: The changes they are in, newest first (`#N`, else a 10-character commit id)

list.description: The list `records` indexes: `protected_edits` for the ratification signals

next.description: The next action a reviewer takes

description: The records `discipline audit --json` prints: one per escape hatch a merged change carried, read from git objects only. A record says what was claimed or applied, not whether a check honoured it.

by_gate.description: Gate id (or configuration table) -> record count

changes_with_records.description: Changes that carried at least one record

checks.description: Every question the audit asks, with its state: a signal is `found` or `clean`; what git alone cannot tell is `not-checked`

changes.description: Changes whose merged pull request was looked up

error.description: The first error, when one failed

failed.description: Changes the forge could not answer for; any makes the forge checks `not-checked`

pulls.description: Of those, the ones that arrived through one

identities.description: For each change with a record or a protected edit, newest first: whether anything records that an agent made it. A missing record is `no-record`, never a person

agent_login.description: Its pull request's author is an agent login; absent without `--forge` or a pull request

marker.description: A `commit-provenance` agent marker matched the commit's trailers or author

state.description: `agent-login`: with `--forge`, its pull request was opened by an `agent_logins` or `[bot]` login; `claimed`: a commit carries a `commit-provenance` agent marker, asserted by the commit and verified by nothing; `no-record`: neither

issues.description: The issues waivers cite, read with `--forge`; empty otherwise

closed_at.description: When it was closed, seconds since the Unix epoch

error.description: Why the forge could not answer

reference.description: The reference as written in a reason

repo.description: The repository it was looked up in; empty for another repository

links.description: Web links from the `origin` remote's forge (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo); null when the remote names none. No request is made

commit.description: A commit's page, `{sha}` for its id

file.description: A file at a commit: `{sha}`, `{path}`, `{line}` (drop `#L{line}` without a line)

file_diff.description: One file's diff in a commit: `{sha}`, `{path_sha256}`; GitHub only

pull.description: A pull request's page, `{n}` for its number

protected_edits.description: Edits to paths the change's parent configuration protects under `ratified-paths` (`kind` `protected-edit`, `detail` `gate on` or `gate off`); with `--forge` each carries its `ratification`

pulls.description: Each change's merged pull request, read with `--forge`; empty otherwise. Logins are not carried

approved_by_other.description: A login other than the pull request's author approved its head

body_edited_after_merge.description: Its body was edited after the merge (GitHub's `lastEditedAt`), so the directives read from it now may not be the ones the gates read; absent when not known

reference.description: The ref audited, as given or defaulted

schema_version.description: This schema's version: a field added keeps it, one renamed, removed or retyped raises it

signals.description: Queries over the records that found something, most urgent first. Review prompts, not verdicts

tightenings.description: Tightenings of `discipline.toml` (`kind` `config-tightening`), newest first: `before` is the looser value

tip.description: The commit the ref resolved to

version.description: The discipline version that wrote the report

title: DisciplineAudit
